questions.skill: Explain ASA congruence with rigid motions
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D, AB = DE, and ∠B ≅ ∠E. Explain, using rigid motions, why △ABC ≅ △DEF.
questions.prompt_markup: In △ABC and △DEF, ∠A ≅ ∠D, AB = DE, and ∠B ≅ ∠E. Explain, using rigid motions, why △ABC ≅ △DEF.
questions.correct_answer: A translation, a rotation, and possibly a reflection carry A to D, B to E, and C to F.
questions.required_method: Translate A to D; rotate so ray AB lies on ray DE (B lands on E); reflect across DE if needed; then use the two angles to place rays AC and BC on rays DF and EF.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: (1) A → D and B → E using AB = DE; (2) C on F's side of DE (reflect if needed); (3) ray AC lands on ray DF because ∠A ≅ ∠D; (4) ray BC lands on ray EF because ∠B ≅ ∠E; (5) C is where rays AC and BC meet, so it lands where DF and EF meet, which is F. Invalid: using side lengths AC or BC (not given); citing ASA to prove ASA.
